paper.title: Repeated Bilateral Trade Against a Smoothed Adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adversary, full feedback, single price
unmapped: Bilateral trade: learner posts price(s) in [0,1] to a seller and buyer; reward is gain from trade (b_t - q)+(p - s_t) if s_t <= p <= q <= b_t
Adaptive adversary chooses each round a sigma-smooth distribution of (S_t,B_t) on [0,1]^2
Learner posts a single price p_t = q_t (strong budget balance); observes (s_t,b_t)
settings.definition_quote: The adversary privately chooses the $\sigma$-smooth distribution of an r.v.\ $(S_t,B_t)$ on $[0,1]^2$ ... Full feedback. $z_t = (s_t,b_t)$: The learner observes both seller and buyer valuations.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adversary, two-bit feedback, single price (lower bound)
unmapped: Bilateral trade with gain-from-trade reward; sigma-smooth adversary over (S_t,B_t)
Two-bit feedback: learner observes I{s_t <= p_t} and I{q_t <= b_t}
Learner restricted to post a single price p_t = q_t
settings.definition_quote: \item{\textbf{Two-bit feedback.}} $z_t = \brb{ \I\{s_t \le p_t\}, \,\I\{q_t \le b_t\} }$: The learner observes separately if the two agents accept the prices offered to each of them.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adversary, two-bit feedback, two prices (lower bound)
unmapped: Bilateral trade with gain-from-trade reward; sigma-smooth adversary over (S_t,B_t)
Two-bit feedback: learner observes I{s_t <= p_t} and I{q_t <= b_t}
Learner may post two prices p_t <= q_t (weak budget balance)
settings.definition_quote: Two-price mechanisms. ... it can post two different prices, $p_t$ to the seller and $q_t$ to the buyer, as long as $p_t\le q_t$ at each time step.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated bilateral trade against a sigma-smooth adaptive adversary, one-bit feedback, two prices
unmapped: Bilateral trade with gain-from-trade reward; adaptive sigma-smooth adversary over (S_t,B_t)
One-bit feedback: learner observes only I{s_t <= p_t <= q_t <= b_t}
Learner may post two prices p_t <= q_t (weak budget balance)
settings.definition_quote: One-bit feedback. $z_t = \I\{s_t \le p_t \le q_t \le b_t\}$: The learner only observes whether or not the trade occurs.

symbols.sigma_s: smoothness parameter sigma in (0,1] of the adversary's distributions
symbols.K_grid: number of points of the uniform price grid used by the algorithm

conditions: sigma-smooth adaptive adversary with sigma in (0,1]

source.label: thm:full-upper
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary in the full feedback model, for any $\sigma \in (0,1]$. Then the regret of \fullfed{}, run using the uniform $K$-grid $G$ on $[0,1]$, for $K \ge 2$, satisfies: $R_T(\mathrm{\shortfullfed}) \le 2\sqrt{T \ln K} + \frac{T}{\sigma K}$.

results.notes: Regret is max over fixed price pairs of expected cumulative GFT difference.

symbols.sigma_s: smoothness parameter sigma in (0,1] of the adversary's distributions

conditions: sigma-smooth adaptive adversary with sigma in (0,1]

source.label: thm:full-upper
source.quote: In particular, for $K = \big\lfloor{\sqrt{T}}\big\rfloor$, the bound becomes: $R_T\mathrm{(\shortfullfed}) \le \frac{4}{\sigma} \cdot \sqrt{T \ln T}$.

results.notes: Tuned version of r1; implicitly requires floor(sqrt T) >= 2.

conditions: any learning algorithm that posts a single price per time step
holds even if S_1, B_1, S_2, ... is an independent family of random variables (oblivious adversary)

source.label: thm:two-bit-one-price-lower
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary in the two-bit feedback model, for any $\sigma \le \tfrac{1}{64}$. Then any learning algorithm that posts a single price per time step suffers at least $\tfrac{T}{24}$ regret, even if $S_1, B_1, S_2, \dots$ is an independent family of random variables.

results.notes: Also implies linear regret for one-bit feedback with a single price.

conditions: any learning algorithm that posts two prices per time step
hard instances are i.i.d. (oblivious) sigma-smooth adversaries

source.label: thm:two-bit-two-prices-lower
source.quote: Consider the problem of repeated bilateral trade against a $\sigma$-smooth adversary in the two-bit feedback model, for any $\sigma \le \tfrac 19$. If $T \ge 8008$, then any learning algorithm $\cA$ that posts two prices per time step suffers at least a regret of $R_T(\cA) \ge \frac{1}{50^3}T \;.$

results.notes: The theorem statement as printed says (1/50^3) T, but the abstract, table, section title and proof all establish (1/50^3) T^{3/4}; the printed T is a typo (a linear lower bound would contradict Theorem 4), so T^{3/4} is recorded. Also applies to one-bit feedback (less informative).

symbols.sigma_s: smoothness parameter sigma in (0,1] of the adversary's distributions
symbols.K_grid: number of points of the uniform price grid

conditions: sigma-smooth adaptive adversary with sigma in (0,1]
tuning: gamma in (0,1), eta > 0, uniform K-grid with 2*eta*K/gamma <= 1

source.label: thm:one-bit-two-prices-upper
source.quote: If we run \blindExpThree{} with exploration rate $\gamma \in (0,1)$, learning rate $\eta >0$, and the uniform $K$-grid $G$ such that $\frac{2\eta K}{\gamma} \le 1$, then, for each time horizon $T \in \N$, we have that $R_T(\text{\blindExpThree{}}) \le \frac{\ln K}{\eta} + \brb{ \gamma + \eta\frac{K}{\gamma} + \frac{1}{\sigma K} } T.$

results.notes: Holds for every T for fixed parameters; algorithm does not need sigma.

symbols.sigma_s: smoothness parameter sigma in (0,1] of the adversary's distributions

conditions: sigma-smooth adaptive adversary with sigma in (0,1]

source.label: thm:one-bit-two-prices-upper
source.quote: In particular, if we set the number of grid points $K = \lfl{  T^{1/4} }$, the exploration rate $\gamma = \frac{ (\ln T)^{1/3} }{ T^{1/4} }$, and the learning rate $\eta = \frac{1}{2} \frac{ (\ln T)^{2/3} }{ T^{3/4} }$, then $R_T(\text{\blindExpThree{}}) \le \lrb{ \frac2\sigma + 3 (\ln T)^{1/3} }\cdot T^{3/4} \;.$

results.notes: Tuning does not use sigma. Also applies to two-bit feedback (more informative).
